hints: From prime factorization n=product(p_i^e_i), each divisor chooses an exponent from 0 to e_i.
The divisor count is product(e_i+1); the divisor sum is product(1+p+...+p^e).
The product of all divisors is n^(divisorCount/2); compute its exponent modulo MOD-1, handling odd divisor count by pairing.
analogy: Every divisor pairs with its complementary divisor n/d, so their product is n; only the square-root divisor needs special handling.
example: For n=12, its six divisors multiply to 1*2*3*4*6*12=1728=12^3.
complexity: O(r log MOD) modular work for r prime factors and O(1) extra space.
correctness: Prime factorization makes divisor count and sum independent products. Every divisor pairs with n/d; if D is even all pair products contribute n, while odd D means every prime exponent is even and the square-root divisor is handled by using exponent (a/2)*D.
algorithm: For each prime power p^a, multiply divisor count D by (a+1) and divisor sum by (1+p+...+p^a), reducing modulo MOD. For the divisor product, compute D modulo 2*(MOD-1) so both parity and D/2 modulo MOD-1 are known. If D is even, the exponent of p is a*(D/2); if D is odd, all a are even and it is (a/2)*D. Reduce exponents modulo MOD-1 and multiply p^exponent modulo MOD.
